coverage_note: Building permits issued by the City of Asheville - Asheville only. Buncombe County's own (unincorporated) permits have no published feed, and the county's other towns publish separately, so totals here are City of Asheville totals, labeled as such. The city publishes no true issue date: this report counts permits that stand in a status proving issuance (issued, certificate issued, finaled, reissued, closed, expired, or temporary certificate issued), by the month each permit was opened. Record types that authorize no building work (short-term home stays, sound exceedance, temporary publishing) are not counted. The city's stated job value is blank or zero on effectively every record, so this report publishes permit counts only. The permit register's record-name field often names a person and is never pulled; a business name is shown only where the city's published business name carries a business signal - individual-looking names are dropped, never printed as a contractor.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one record_id in the City of Asheville's AccelaPermitsView layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Scoped trailing-12-month window (date_opened >= 2025-11-26, date_opened <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, issued-proven status scope + non-building category exclusions - see pull_where_extra), measured 2026-11-26 on a full paged audit pull: 2,985 rows = 2,985 distinct record_id, 0 duplicates, 0 null record_ids. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: address, as published by the city - the full printed address including city, state, and ZIP (e.g. '22 EVELAKE DR, ASHEVILLE, NC 28806'), carried verbatim, never inferred. Present on all 2,985 scoped permits.
field_map.application_date: date_opened (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date) - the date the permit application was opened with the city.
field_map.category: From record_type_type, the city's own class: Residential publishes Residential (1,261 scoped permits) and Commercial publishes Commercial (806); the remaining classes (Event-Temporary Use, Fire, Sign, Over The Counter, Stormwater, Outdoor Vendor, Right of Way) publish no residential/commercial class and stay NULL, never inferred.
field_map.contractor_rule: business_name ONLY, and only when the value carries a business signal: a legal-form marker (LLC, INC, CORP, CORPORATION, PARTNERSHIP, COMPANY, DBA, AKA, or a trailing CO.), a trade or business keyword (ELECTRIC, PLUMBING, CONSTRUCTION, ROOFING, SERVICES, and the classifier's documented keyword set in normalize_asheville), an ampersand or slash or digit, or a single-token trade name. A plain multi-word name with no business signal reads as an individual (the register's applicants include licensed sole operators filing under their own names) and is dropped to NULL, never published as a contractor. Measured at build on the scoped window: 2,211 of 2,985 permits state a business_name; 2,108 values carried, 103 dropped as individual-looking (70 distinct names). The rule is deliberately conservative: it also drops a handful of real businesses whose names carry no signal, rather than risk printing one person's name. record_name - often a PERSON name - is excluded from pull_select entirely and never requested.
field_map.issue_date: date_opened, LABELED AS SUCH. The feed publishes no issuance date: its other dates are the record's current-status date and workflow dates (assigned/closed/completed), none of which is an issuance date. Published counts are therefore permits that have been issued (status evidence), counted in the month the application was opened; recent months grow as opened applications complete review and reach an issued status. This definition is printed on the county hub, the Data Sources page, and llms.txt (the Fort Worth treatment).
field_map.permit_number: record_id - verified exactly unique in the scoped window (2,985 distinct = 2,985 rows, 2026-11-26 audit pull).
field_map.permit_type_source: record_type, the city's own permit type (e.g. 'Res: Alterations', 'Com: Demo', 'Stand Alone Sign'), with record_type_category, record_type_type, and record_type_subtype - the city's type hierarchy - carried in the pull for trade classification and category only.
field_map.project_description: description, the city's own scope text (rich free text on the scoped permits).
field_map.scope_filter: The register is the city's all-applications Accela view (66,667 rows all-time). pull_where_extra keeps only permits standing in a status that proves issuance - record_status IN ('Issued','CC Issued','CO Issued','Finaled','Reissued','Closed','Expired','TCO Issued 30 Days','TCO Issued 60 Days','TCO Issued 90 Days','TCC Issued 90 Days') - and excludes the non-building record_type_category values 'Home Stay', 'Sound Exceedance', and 'TempPub'. On the trailing-12-month opened window (3,672 rows), the status scope and category exclusions leave 2,985 published permits. Every excluded status and category is named here and on the Data Sources page (the Fort Worth/Alachua treatment).
field_map.status: record_status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Only issued-proven statuses enter the population at all (see scope_filter): Issued, CC Issued, CO Issued, Reissued, and the TCO/TCC temporary-certificate statuses publish as issued; Finaled and Closed as complete; Expired as expired.
field_map.valuation: COUNTS-ONLY, enforced by construction: the layer's job_value field is > 0 on only 3 of 66,667 records all-time and 0 of 2,985 scoped records (measured 2026-11-26 against the live layer), so there is no figure to validate or publish. job_value is not requested in pull_select at all: no dollar figure enters our data, none is published or aggregated (verified: zero '$' totals on the county's pages), and none is estimated. The reason is stated openly on the hub, the Data Sources page, and in llms.txt.

freshness_stamp_where: date_opened <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AND record_status IN ('Issued','CC Issued','CO Issued','Finaled','Reissued','Closed','Expired','TCO Issued 30 Days','TCO Issued 60 Days','TCO Issued 90 Days','TCC Issued 90 Days') AND record_type_category NOT IN ('Home Stay','Sound Exceedance','TempPub')
history_range: 66,667 rows all-time in the view at build (date_opened 2014-01-02 onward); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Public access via the City of Asheville's official GIS services; attribution: City of Asheville, North Carolina
pull_where_extra: date_opened <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AND record_status IN ('Issued','CC Issued','CO Issued','Finaled','Reissued','Closed','Expired','TCO Issued 30 Days','TCO Issued 60 Days','TCO Issued 90 Days','TCC Issued 90 Days') AND record_type_category NOT IN ('Home Stay','Sound Exceedance','TempPub')
rate_limit: ArcGIS FeatureServer query, 200,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: City of Asheville open data - Accela Permits View
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-26: the AccelaPermitsView layer is published by the City of Asheville on the city's official GIS server (gis.ashevillenc.gov) with public access, and the same layer is cataloged in the city's ArcGIS Online organization (item 'City of Asheville Permit Inspections', owner AVLGIS). Figures are published 'as reported by the City of Asheville' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Live Accela view (records opened and statused the same day); MEASURED 2026-11-26: all-time max date_opened 2026-11-26 and max record_status_date 2026-11-26. The layer publishes no editingInfo stamp, so freshness (gate 5) is measured as the freshest scoped record_status_date (2026-11-26T04:30Z at build) under a 96h threshold.
watermark_field: date_opened + record_id - refresh re-pulls the full trailing-12-month window nightly and upserts: the feed's records change status IN PLACE (an application opened in the window enters the published set when it reaches an issued-proven status), so a watermark-only pull would miss status transitions; the full-window re-pull is this registry's refresh shape (the Fort Worth treatment; gate 4's count baseline is computed on the identical where).
